rfi.title: Fifteen years of independence for South Sudan, but still little to celebrate
rfi.description: South Sudan, the world's youngest country, on Thursday marks the 15th anniversary of its independence, following decades of war with Sudan, a 2005 peace agreement and a 2011 self-determination referendum in which almost 99 percent of voters backed statehood. But the hopes that came with it have given way to renewed conflict, economic collapse and political deadlock.

rfi.title: Favourites France head into Morocco rematch banking on Mbappé magic
rfi.description: France storm into Thursday's World Cup quarter-final against Morocco as the tournament's hot favourites.

rfi.title: UK to lead European initiative to fund next generation of long-range missiles
rfi.description: The United Kingdom, France, Germany and other European countries will spend more than $50 billion over the next 10 years to develop long-range precision weapons in a boost to NATO's defence capabilities, the UK government announced on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Secrecy surrounds Bayeux Tapestry's imminent Channel crossing
rfi.description: Under cover of darkness and heavy police guard, the Bayeux Tapestry – a 68-metre embroidered chronicle of the Norman conquest of England, stitched in wool not long after the events it depicts – is set to cross the Channel within days, the official overseeing its move to London has revealed.

rfi.title: How appeal court verdict against Le Pen puts her back in the running for 2027
rfi.description: A French appeals court this week upheld Marine Le Pen's conviction for embezzling funds from the European Parliament and sentenced her to house arrest – something the far-right leader previously said would rule her out of France's 2027 presidential race. Yet Le Pen still has one last legal recourse to overturn her conviction and, pending that appeal, remains free to hit the campaign trail.

rfi.title: Trump says US will give Ukraine licence to build Patriot missiles
rfi.description: The United States will grant Ukraine a licence to manufacture Patriot missile interceptors domestically, President Donald Trump announced from this week's NATO summit – as Kyiv's stockpile of the US-made air defence system runs critically low amid intensifying Russian strikes.

rfi.title: Zimbabwe's ruling party accused of hollowing out parliamentary oversight
rfi.description: Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa has signed into law constitutional changes extending his time in office from 2028 to 2030. The legislation, known as CAB3, also allows parliament, rather than a public vote, to elect future presidents.

rfi.title: Western Europe records hottest ever June as climate change drives heatwaves
rfi.description: Western Europe experienced its warmest June on record, as a heatwave at the end of the month in many countries broke temperature records. The confirmation from the European Union’s climate monitor comes as many countries are facing a third heatwave this week since May.

rfi.title: 'We have our own local identity’: Morocco's Jazzablanca festival founder
rfi.description: As the Jazzablanca festival celebrates its 19th edition, RFI spoke to its founder Moulay Ahmed Alami about how the event has evolved, its support for Moroccan artists and the wider cultural and economic impact on Casablanca.

rfi.title: Ugandan farmers take TotalEnergies' pipeline to UK court

rfi.title: Trump lashes out at NATO allies over Greenland and Iran, targeting Spain
rfi.description: United States President Donald Trump lashed out at NATO allies on Wednesday at the organisations's summit in Ankara, as the fallout from his war on Iran threatened to overshadow the gathering.

rfi.title: Macron says Syria must not be destabilised after bombs wound 18
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron warned on Tuesday that Syria must not be destabilised after twin bomb attacks near the Damascus hotel where he spent the night, during a landmark state visit to a country emerging from years of civil war.

rfi.title: Kenya journalist escapes abduction after criticism of president, says CPJ
rfi.description: The Committee to Protect Journalists has called for an investigation into the attempted kidnapping of a senior journalist in Kenya, which followed angry criticism of his newspaper by President William Ruto.

rfi.title: Submarine missile test puts China's Pacific ambitions on display
rfi.description: A Chinese submarine test-fired a "strategic" missile carrying a dummy warhead into the Pacific Ocean on Monday, Beijing said, prompting immediate condemnation across the region.

rfi.title: Egyptian football chiefs hit out at World Cup referees following last-16 exit
rfi.description: The Egyptian Football Association (EFA) on Wednesday lodged a formal complaint with World Cup organisers Fifa over the officiating during the team's defeat to defending champions Argentina on Tuesday in the last-16 at the 2026 World Cup.

rfi.title: Greenland 'not for sale', Danish PM says at NATO summit
rfi.description: Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said Wednesday that Greenland was "not for sale" following remarks by President Donald Trump suggesting the territory should be controlled by Washington and not Copenhagen.

rfi.title: Oil prices continue to rally as US and Iran step up mutual attacks
rfi.description: Oil prices jumped more than 3 percent on Wednesday as the Middle East crisis burst back into the spotlight, with United States and Iranian forces exchanging strikes after attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, fuelling fresh supply fears.

rfi.title: Switzerland beat Colombia on penalties to set up last-eight date with Argentina
rfi.description: Switzerland beat Colombia in a penalty shootout on Tuesday to advance to the last eight at the World Cup for the first time since 1954. They will play Argentina on Saturday in Kansas City.

lemonde.title: « Il a la vie devant lui » : après un an à penser à l’Elysée, Jordan Bardella ramené à sa condition de numéro deux
lemonde.description: Le président du Rassemblement national a affiché un visage fermé lors de la première sortie de précampagne de Marine Le Pen, qu’il n’a pas même félicitée pour sa candidature à l’élection présidentielle de 2027. La décision de justice du 7 juillet dans l’affaire des assistants parlementaires européens devrait trancher les querelles de ligne.

lemonde.title: Au sommet de l’OTAN, Donald Trump alterne menaces et effusions, rassure ses alliés et apporte un nouveau soutien à l’Ukraine
lemonde.description: En Turquie, le président américain, après avoir critiqué l’Espagne et rappelé ses visées sur le Groenland, a assuré de son engagement en faveur de la clause d’assistance mutuelle de l’Alliance et autorisé Kiev à produire sous licence des missiles Patriot.

lemonde.title: Le Haut Conseil pour le climat alerte sur l’urgence de « changer d’échelle » dans les politiques climatiques
lemonde.description: Alors que la France subit une troisième canicule en moins de deux mois, l’instance dénonce le ralentissement de la décarbonation et les reculs de certaines politiques environnementales. Elle juge que le pays n’est pas préparé aux impacts croissants du réchauffement.

lemonde.title: Entre l’Iran et les Etats-Unis, la reprise des hostilités illustre la grande défiance de Téhéran vis-à-vis des négociations
lemonde.description: Les échanges de frappes entre les deux pays depuis la nuit de mardi à mercredi donnent des arguments à la frange ultraconservatrice du régime théocratique, qui considère les discussions avec Washington comme vaines, voire criminelles. Le cessez-le-feu ne tient plus qu’à un fil.

lemonde.title: Aux Etats-Unis, la chute du démocrate Graham Platner menace d’empêcher le parti d’emporter le Sénat
lemonde.description: Le candidat aux sénatoriales de novembre dans l’Etat du Maine, représentant de l’aile gauche populiste qui bouscule le Parti démocrate, a dû jeter l’éponge, mercredi, après une série de scandales.

lemonde.title: France-Maroc : la soif de revanche des Lions de l’Atlas, quatre ans après la demi-finale perdue au Qatar
lemonde.description: La sélection marocaine de football n’a battu la France qu’une seule fois, lors d’un tournoi amical, en mai 1998. Vingt-huit ans plus tard, ses supporteurs ont des raisons de croire en une victoire de leur équipe, plus forte que jamais, en quarts de finale du Mondial 2026.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : vote décisif au PS pour sceller le sort de la primaire unitaire
lemonde.description: Les militants du Parti socialiste se prononcent, jeudi, sur la méthode de départage de leur future tête d’affiche pour 2027. La « primaire de la gauche » incluant Les Ecologistes et les anciens « insoumis » n’est plus à l’ordre du jour.

lemonde.title: Le gouvernement débloque en urgence des aides pour les agriculteurs, frappés par la flambée des prix des engrais
lemonde.description: L’exécutif a annoncé un plan d’aides de près de 150 millions d’euros aux agriculteurs pour leur permettre de surmonter la crise des engrais qui les touche depuis quelques mois. En grande partie fabriqués dans le golfe Arabo-Persique, les prix se sont envolés d’environ 30 % au premier semestre, au moment où les cours des produits agricoles sont restés très bas.

lemonde.title: L’Arcom met CNews en demeure pour la troisième fois depuis le début de l’année
lemonde.description: L’Autorité de régulation de la communication audiovisuelle et numérique estime que la chaîne du groupe Bolloré a manqué de mesure et d’honnêté dans un reportage consacré à Rachida Dati diffusé l’avant-veille du deuxième tour des élections municipales, en mars 2026.

lemonde.title: La contrôleuse générale des lieux de privation de liberté dénonce les « violences systémiques » pratiquées contre les détenus à la prison de Condé-sur-Sarthe
lemonde.description: Dans un rapport publié jeudi 9 juillet, l’autorité indépendante alerte sur une « logique d’intimidation et d’abus de pouvoir » des surveillants, dans le quartier de lutte contre la criminalité, mais aussi des propos racistes, au sein de la prison de l’Orne.

lemonde.title: Logement : le Sénat adopte un projet de loi renforcé de mesures d’adaptation aux canicules
lemonde.description: Saisie dans un délai très court, la chambre haute a enrichi le texte gouvernemental qui ambitionne d’accroître l’offre de logements neufs ou rénovés et de décentraliser certaines compétences, en ajoutant quelques propositions relatives au « confort d’été ».

lemonde.title: Séismes au Venezuela : le bilan monte à 3 811 morts, la présidente demande au roi d’Angleterre le déblocage de l’or du pays
lemonde.description: Alors que les besoins humanitaires restent considérables, Caracas poursuit ses démarches pour obtenir la levée des restrictions sur ses avoirs gelés à l’étranger. Les Nations unies évaluent les pertes provoquées par les séismes à 6,7 milliards de dollars.

lemonde.title: Un lanceur d’alerte à l’origine de révélations sur la machine de propagande russe en Centrafrique se voit refuser l’asile en France
lemonde.description: De 2019 à 2022, Ephrem Yalike-Ngonzo a participé à des campagnes de désinformation pour le compte du groupe de sécurité privé russe Wagner en Centrafrique. Il a pu rejoindre la France en 2024 avec le soutien des autorités françaises.

lemonde.title: Quand l’assureur tarde à faire une offre d’indemnisation à la victime d’un accident de la circulation
lemonde.description: Le non-respect des délais prévus par la loi Badinter entraîne le doublement du taux d’intérêt légal sur les sommes dues.

lemonde.title: Tour de France 2026 : entre classement général et victoire d’étape, le cœur des coureurs balance
lemonde.description: Pour prendre une échappée, les coureurs en quête d’un bouquet doivent d’abord perdre du temps au classement général. Une situation difficile à accepter au sein du peloton pour ceux capables de jouer sur les deux tableaux.

lemonde.title: Festival d’Avignon : avec « Growing Piece », la chorégraphe Madeleine Fournier livre un étonnant récit de réincarnation
lemonde.description: La danseuse interprète son nouveau spectacle inspiré par la mythologie grecque, en duo avec le joueur de cornemuse Julien Desailly, à partir du 10 juillet.

euronews.description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde rejected claims in an exclusive interview with Euronews that the digital euro is designed to replace cash or allow the central bank to monitor payments, as the legislation entered a new phase following months of talks in the European Parliament.

euronews.description: In 2013, Syria agreed to join the OPCW and disclose and hand over its toxic stockpile under Russian and US pressure and to avert the threat of air strikes by Washington and its allies.

euronews.title: Portuguese rapper jailed in Germany for drug trafficking is deported to Portugal
euronews.description: Ivo Vieira Silva, better known as rapper 18 Karat, was deported early on Wednesday. Sentenced in Dec 2022 to six years and three months, he will remain free in Portugal, but any return to Germany would mean immediate arrest to serve the rest of his term.

euronews.title: Santas fill Danish streets for annual congress
euronews.description: Dozens of Santas and Mrs. Clauses gather in Aalborg, Denmark, for the World Santa Claus Congress, with parades, family activities and summer festivities.

euronews.title: News outlets seek sanctions against OpenAI in copyright battle
euronews.description: OpenAI has been "hiding and destroying evidence" of how it trained ChatGPT on copyrighted news content, US media organisations allege as legal costs in the landmark copyright battle top $28 million.

euronews.description: BBVA was placed under investigation in July 2019 for allegedly hiring a private investigation agency to spy on politicians, journalists and business figures.

euronews.description: In an Euronews opinion piece, MEP Nikos Papandreou urges the EU to press Egypt to end discrimination against the Baha'i community. He argues Cairo should honour its constitutional commitment to freedom of belief by granting Baha'is equal legal rights.

euronews.title: EU set to greenlight Hungary's €10 billion recovery envelope
euronews.description: The decision would pave the way for the release of post-pandemic funds that had long been withheld over corruption concerns.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le quart de finale France-Maroc vu par les Marocains à Boston
france24fr.description: Boston abrite une importante communauté marocaine, l'une des plus grandes des États-Unis. Et elle était mobilisée pour assister au quart de finale contre la France.

france24fr.title: "Ce sera une revanche" : les Bleus ont les yeux tournés vers la demi-finale du Mondial 2026
france24fr.description: Après leur victoire en quarts de finale de la Coupe du monde 2026 face au Maroc, les Bleus se tournent désormais vers leur prochain adversaire, pour la phase suivante de la compétition. Mais ils restent réalistes sur leurs capacités et leur potentiel.

france24fr.title: Un feu de forêt fait au moins 12 morts près d'Almeria, dans le sud de l'Espagne
france24fr.description: Un incendie s'est déclaré jeudi après-midi à Los Gallardos, en Andalousie. Le gouvernement régional a fait état d'un bilan de 12 morts, quand quelque 150 pompiers et cinq camions-citernes sont mobilisés pour lutter contre les flammes.

france24fr.title: Kylian Mbappé revient sur son penalty et le contexte de sa frappe captée par le gardien marocain
france24fr.description: L'attaquant français Kylian Mbappé est revenu, après le match France-Maroc, sur le contexte de son penalty capté par le gardien marocain Yassine Bounou. "Un scénario qu'il va falloir envisager", relativise le joueur.

france24fr.title: "Il y a beaucoup de choses à améliorer" : après le Maroc, les Bleus veulent rester concentrés
france24fr.description: L'équipe de France a surmonté l'obstacle du Maroc (2-0) pour rallier le dernier carré de la Coupe du monde 2026. Pourtant, interrogés en zone mixte, Kylian Mbappé, Ousmane Dembélé et Warren Zaïre-Emery affirment surtout penser à la suite. Réactions.

france24fr.title: En direct : le guide suprême Khamenei inhumé sur fond de frappes
france24fr.description: Le défunt guide suprême iranien Ali Khamenei a été inhumé tôt vendredi à Machhad, a rapporté la télévision d'État, après plusieurs jours de funérailles marquées par la reprise des hostilités entre les États-Unis et l'Iran. La cérémonie a eu lieu sans la présence apparente de son fils et successeur, Mojtaba Khamenei, selon les images diffusées par la télévision d'État. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: La Syrie annonce l'arrestation de responsables des explosions à Damas, une cellule "affiliée à l'EI"
france24fr.description: Les autorités syriennes ont annoncé jeudi l'arrestation des responsables des deux attentats à la bombe survenus mardi à Damas pendant la visite d'Emmanuel Macron. "Les premières investigations ont montré que la cellule était affiliée à l'organisation EI", a précisé le chef de la sécurité intérieure pour la région de Damas, à la télévision d'État.

france24fr.title: "Je crois en moi" : Warren Zaïre-Emery prêt à rentrer plus longtemps sur le terrain
france24fr.description: Le milieu de terrain français Warren Zaïre-Emery a joué ce jeudi 9 juillet son premier match lors du Mondial 2026 en rentrant en seconde période face au Maroc. Après la rencontre remportée 2-0 par la France, le joueur, visiblement ému, s'est dit confiant en ses capacités et la possibilité de se retrouver plus sur le terrain.

france24fr.title: Regain des hostilités entre l'Iran et les États-Unis avant l'inhumation d'Ali Khamenei
france24fr.description: L'armée américaine a mené de nouvelles frappes contre l'Iran dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi afin de garantir la navigation dans le détroit d'Ormuz, provoquant des ripostes de Téhéran qui a ciblé des sites au Koweït, au Qatar et à Bahreïn. Par la voix de son ministre de la Défense, Israël s'est dit prêt à attaquer l'Iran "une troisième fois si nécessaire".

france24fr.title: Canicule : l'été de tous les dangers ?
france24fr.description: La France traverse sa troisième canicule en moins de deux mois. Dans le même temps, des incendies d'une ampleur exceptionnelle ravagent plusieurs régions : en seulement huit jours, 8 000 hectares sont partis en fumée, soit davantage que sur l'ensemble du mois de juillet l'an dernier. Face à cette situation, le Haut Conseil pour le climat tire la sonnette d'alarme et appelle à « changer d'échelle » dans les politiques climatiques.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Mbappé et Dembélé font sauter le verrou marocain pour hisser la France en demi-finale
Mondial 2026 : Mbappé et Dembélé font sauter le verrou marocain pour hisser la France en demi-finale
france24fr.description: La France a éliminé le Maroc jeudi 9 juillet à Boston, en quarts de finale de la Coupe du monde 2026. Après avoir longtemps buté sur un excellent Yassine Bounou, Kylian Mbappé et Ousmane Dembélé ont finalement trouvé la faille pour hisser les Bleus dans le dernier carré (2-0).

france24fr.title: OTAN: Donald Trump critique... et tempère
france24fr.description: Le sommet de l'OTAN a pris fin dans la capitale turque, Ankara. Une réunion une nouvelle fois bousculée par Donald Trump. Le président des Etats-Unis a réitéré ses griefs contre ses alliés, notamment de ne pas l'avoir soutenu dans sa guerre contre l'Iran. Mais il autorise l'Ukraine à fabriquer des Patriot, ces missiles américains de défense anti-aérienne. C'était une demande de longue date de l'Ukraine.

france24fr.title: Iran : des frappes et des funérailles
france24fr.description: Après six jours de deuil national, l'ancien guide suprême iranien Ali Khamenei a été inhumé dans sa ville natale de Machad. Sur le passage de son cercueil, des milliers de personnes rassemblées. Dans les cortèges : des appels à tuer Donald Trump alors que les Etats-Unis ont lancé près d'une centaine de frappes sur l'Iran. De quoi remettre en cause l'accord signé il y a trois semaines entre les deux pays ?

france24fr.title: Insultes, affaire Mbappé, IA… Est-ce la "Coupe du monde du racisme" ?
france24fr.description: Après le match entre l'Argentine et l'Egypte que les Pharaons accusent d'être truqué, une image devenue virale sur les réseaux sociaux prétend montrer les Lions de l’Atlas solidaires du sélectionneur égyptien Hossam Hassan à travers le geste "Non au racisme". Si ce sont en réalité de vieilles images décontextualisées, elles n'empêchent pas une vérité : une vague de racisme déferle sur les réseaux sociaux lors de cette édition 2026, dont Kylian Mbappé a notamment été victime.

france24fr.title: Le pronostic d'AT Frenchies pour France-Maroc
france24fr.description: Nos journalistes ont croisé les influenceurs AT Frenchies et leur ont posé LA question : qui va gagner ce soir entre le Maroc et la France ? Voici leur pronostic pour ce quart de finale de la Coupe du monde

france24fr.title: Le Conseil constitutionnel sénégalais invalide la réforme révisant l'équilibre des pouvoirs
france24fr.description: Le Conseil constitutionnel du Sénégal a invalidé jeudi un texte de loi adopté la semaine dernière par l'Assemblée nationale, révisant l'équilibre des pouvoirs entre exécutif et parlement. Cette décision est le dernier rebondissement en date dans le conflit qui oppose le président Bassirou Diomaye Faye à l'Assemblée nationale dirigée par Ousmane Sonko.

france24fr.title: L'Italie expulse deux espions accusés de livrer des informations à Moscou
france24fr.description: L'Italie a ordonné jeudi l'expulsion de deux espions russes sous couverture diplomatique, a annoncé le ministre des Affaires étrangères Antonio Tajani, condamnant une "ingérence grave et inacceptable" de Moscou. L'expulsion survient deux jours après l'arrestation de deux anciens agents des services de renseignement italiens qui auraient transmis à la Russie des informations concernant l'aide militaire à l'Ukraine.

zeit.description: In der Nähe von Almería im Süden von Spanien ist ein Feuer ausgebrochen. Zwölf Menschen starben. Die Regionalregierung spricht von einer »beispiellosen Tragödie«.

zeit.description: Im Wochenendpodcast erzählt die Künstlerin Cihan Çakmak, wie sie ihre Bergamottenbäume pflegt. Und schwärmt von ihren Lieblingsorten in Lissabon.

nzz.description: Markus Ritter ist vielleicht der mächtigste Politiker in Bern. Im Gespräch sagt der Bauernpräsident, warum die verpasste Bundesratswahl für ihn ein Glück ist und was er seiner italienischen Mutter verdankt.

nzz.description: Der Nato-Gipfel in Ankara ist harmonischer verlaufen als erwartet. Wladimir Putin wird ihn genau beobachtet haben.

nzz.title: Die «Wiedergeborene»: Marine Le Pen ist zurück im Rennen um die Präsidentschaft
nzz.description: Marine Le Pen feiert ihr politisches Comeback und startet in den Präsidentschaftswahlkampf. Doch ihre Kandidatur bleibt eine Wette auf Zeit. Und Jordan Bardella? Der ist erst einmal abgemeldet.

nzz.title: China produziert Waren, die in China immer weniger Absatz finden. Dem Land droht ein Rückfall in die Deflation
nzz.description: Neue Inflationsdaten deuten darauf hin, dass sich Chinas Hersteller nicht aus der negativen Preisspirale befreien können. Das dürfte sich auch auf die nationalen Wachstumszahlen auswirken.

nzz.title: Atomkraft oder Solarstrom: Wer braucht mehr Subventionen?
nzz.description: Neue AKW sollen weniger auf staatliche Förderung angewiesen sein als Solaranlagen auf Dächern. Zu diesem Schluss kommt Economiesuisse. Doch die Rechnung stösst auf heftigen Widerspruch.

nzz.title: Der «Zwangsarbeit-Zoll» ist erst der Anfang: Das sind Trumps nächste Schritte im Handelsstreit mit dem Rest der Welt
nzz.description: Am 24. Juli müssen die USA ihr jetziges Zollregime ersetzen. Für Staaten wie die Schweiz dürfte sich die Lage nicht komplett verändern. Später drohen aber unangenehme Überraschungen.

nzz.title: Krieg in Libanon: Die Zerstörung von Kulturstätten ist eine Kriegswaffe
nzz.description: Kaum ein anderes Land des Nahen Ostens vereint auf so engem Raum die Spuren so vieler Zivilisationen wie Libanon. Aber mit dem Fokus auf den jüngsten Krieg zwischen Israel und dem Hizbullah bleiben die Schäden an bedeutenden Kulturstätten in Südlibanon meistens unerwähnt.

nzz.title: «Als hätte eine Private-Equity-Firma ein Kind mit Google bekommen»: Das ist das italienische Einhorn Bending Spoons
nzz.description: Sie kaufen gut eingeführte Internetfirmen und bauen sie um: Wie ein paar «ragazzi» aus einem Mailänder Startup ein globales Unternehmen gemacht und es an die Wall Street gebracht haben. Und was das mit dem Kultfilm «Matrix» zu tun hat.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Der antifaschistische Konsens gegen die AfD ist eine Lüge. Davon profitieren nur Linksextreme und Antisemiten
nzz.description: Die politische Mitte war schon immer naiv gegenüber der radikalen Linken. Sie macht sich zu nützlichen Idioten für Kräfte, die Gewalt propagieren und «Israel verrecke» krakeelen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Houston, die Demokraten haben ein Problem: die radikale Linke
nzz.description: Klassenkampf, militanter Antizionismus: Anti-Establishment-Kandidaten gewinnen Einfluss in der Demokratischen Partei und gefährden ein Comeback an die Schalthebel der Macht in Washington.

nzz.title: «Trump will sicher nicht mit 20 000 Mann in Kuba einmarschieren»
nzz.description: Der Lateinamerika-Experte Bert Hoffmann erklärt, was die Machthaber in Havanna mit ihren Reformplänen erreichen wollen – und warum eine Entführung von Raúl Castro den USA nichts brächte.

nzz.title: «Ein Wort genügt – und schon öffnen sich in der Luft die Tore» – gelebte Literatur in der Ukraine
nzz.description: Das renommierte ukrainische Literaturfestival Meridian hat sich entschlossen, die Veranstaltungen nicht am Stammsitz Czernowitz, sondern in Frontstädten stattfinden zu lassen. Dieses Jahr in Charkiw und Saporischja. Ein beklemmender Augenschein vor Ort.

nzz.title: 50 Jahre nach dem katastrophalen Chemieunfall von Seveso leiden Betroffene immer noch
nzz.description: Im Juli 1976 trat aus einer Fabrik in der Nähe des norditalienischen Ortes Seveso eine Wolke aus giftigem Dioxin aus. Der Unfall brachte Europa neue Umweltrichtlinien und wirkt bis heute nach. Ein Rückblick.

nzz.title: GASTKOMMENTAR - Der Staat sollte nicht Krippen subventionieren, sondern die Erwerbstätigkeit von Eltern fördern
nzz.description: Die neue Betreuungszulage des Bundes belohnt eine bestimmte Betreuungsform, nicht das politische Ziel: Sie subventioniert Krippen, statt erwerbstätige Eltern zu entlasten. Das ist ordnungspolitisch der falsche Hebel und sozialpolitisch ein Eigentor.

nzz.title: Bosch rüstet bei E-Bikes auf
nzz.description: Mit kostenlosem Drehmoment-Upgrade auf 120 Nm und schnellerem Ladegerät versucht der Konzern seine Vormachtstellung auch gegen die Konkurrenz aus China zu verteidigen.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - Ist Strom in Deutschland gerade sauber oder schmutzig?
nzz.description: Die NZZ zeigt in Echtzeit, wie viel Wind, Sonne, Kohle und Gas im Strommix stecken – und wie Deutschland im Vergleich zu seinen Nachbarn dasteht.

observador.description: A Igreja alemã quer mudanças profundas e Roma trava esse caminho. João Francisco Gomes explica o conflito e porque é que há quem tema uma nova divisão na Igreja Católica.

observador.description: José Luís Carneiro diz que facilitam os despejos. Ainda, Montenegro garante "esforço grande" para resolver os  problemas nos exames nacionais.

observador.description: Ciente da preocupação dos alunos e dos professores Luís Montenegro pede confiança. Ainda, França é a primeira seleção qualificada para as meias finais do Campeonato do Mundo.

observador.title: 2h. Jorge Jesus é hoje oficializado como novo selecionador
observador.description: A grande dúvida da apresentação de Jesus será quem o vai acompanhar na equipa técnica. Ainda, a esta hora 6 localidades do concelho de Almada estão sem abastecimento de água.

observador.title: 1h. CM Almada garante que resposta à crise não é de agora
observador.description: Inês de Medeiros diz ainda que já tem um novo furo de captação de água em funcionamento. Ainda, Jorge Jesus vai ser esta sexta-feira oficializado como novo selecionador nacional.

observador.description: Partido acusa ex-Presidente de dirigir "à distância" perseguição ao líder da oposição, detido há oito meses e a aguardar decisão sobre prisão preventiva.

observador.title: Trump tem toda a razão sobre a Europa
observador.description: Desligada dos EUA, esta Europa enfraquecida e desorientada tornar-se-ia rapidamente terra para todas as piratarias políticas. Nunca a Europa, desde o pós-guerra, dependeu tanto da América.

observador.title: A guerra que se senta à mesa com bolsa de estudo
observador.description: Esta guerra não é feita com Kalashnikovs. As suas armas são  ao ombro. Entra com bolsas de investigação para cursos como “Intifada Performativa: Acampar no Campus Contra a Civilização”.

observador.title: A Igreja condenou, ou não, o modernismo?
observador.description: O modernismo e o liberalismo são conceitos demasiado amplos e contraditórios. Não é de espantar, por isso, que a reação da Igreja também o seja.

observador.title: Infanta Sofia faz primeiro discurso com apoio da família
observador.description: A filha mais nova dos Reis de Espanha discursou na quarta-feira numa cerimónia da Fundação Ibercaja, com os pais e a irmã Leonor na plateia, numa surpresa à agenda oficial.

observador.title: O triunfo da justiça
observador.description: A sentença da juíza Daniela Braga de Oliveira honra a magistratura; e o recurso do Ministério Público, mesmo que venha a merecer acolhimento, não é mais de que uma perrice de orgulhozinho ferido.

observador.title: 00h. Falhas água. Autarca de Almada anuncia novos furos
observador.description: Inês de Medeiros garante que a resposta à crise de abastecimento de água não começou a ser dada esta semana. Ainda, França é a primeira seleção qualificada para as meias-finais do Mundial.

observador.title: Quando o Estado é sócio do agiota
observador.description: Na cadeia do crédito ao consumo o agiota não está à margem da lei, está dentro dela, e teve, durante dois anos, o Estado como sócio silencioso.

observador.title: A Beira Baixa não se vende
observador.description: A Beira Baixa não é contra o futuro. Pelo contrário: quer fazer parte dele. Mas não aceitará ser reduzida a uma paisagem de sacrifício para alimentar consumos distantes.

observador.title: Queremos modernizar. Desde que nada mude
observador.description: As falhas devem ser corrigidas e prevenidas. Mas uma implementação imperfeita não transforma uma boa reforma numa má reforma.

observador.description: O Governo não fez, nem quis fazer, qualquer alteração aos direitos de quem não pode trabalhar.

observador.description: O que virá a acontecer no que a Marine Le Pen diz respeito é um mistério, pelo nível de ineditismo e as interrogações quanto à forma como gerir uma realidade perfeitamente anómala.

phys-org.title: Q&A: Examining the Global South's call for environmental justice amid expanding technology
phys-org.description: Digital technologies—from artificial intelligence to smartphones and data centers—are often described as "clean" innovations. Yet every device depends on minerals, electricity, labor and global supply chains, raising important questions about environmental justice and development.

phys-org.title: The Matua people: Sounds and rituals strengthen cross-border sense of community
phys-org.description: Professor Carola Lorea of the University of Tübingen's Department of Social and Cultural Anthropology has published a comprehensive academic study on the Matua, a community of 50 million people scattered across India, Bangladesh and 32 other nations in the wake of evictions and forced migration. Despite national borders and natural barriers such as the Bay of Bengal Delta, swamps and the sea, the community's cohesion has only grown over the decades. Lorea's work represents more th

phys-org.title: From The Godfather to Middlemarch: 8 of the most faithful adaptations ever
phys-org.description: Adapting canonical literary classics into cinema is an inherently difficult task, as it requires walking a razor's edge between remaining faithful to the text and translating it into another medium.

phys-org.title: Morning glories reveal 96% drop in adaptation as pollinator pressure reshapes evolution
phys-org.description: Facing both climate change and a crashing pollinator population, plants may be evolving to attract pollinators rather than adapting to a warming climate, and the trade-off has resulted in a steep decline in plants' rate of adaptation, according to a University of Michigan study. The researchers, studying morning glories, observed a 96% decrease in the population's rate of adaptation over nine years. The declining rate of adaptation could affect farmers, who deal with morning glory as a

phys-org.title: Parents direct more threats toward school administrators than teachers
phys-org.description: In K–12 schools across the country, administrators are tasked with keeping everyone safe. New research shows they may be the most in need of protection.

phys-org.title: AI reveals hidden San Andreas Fault movements
phys-org.description: When people think about geological faults, they usually think about earthquakes. Yet faults do not move only during earthquakes. Sometimes they slip silently, without generating noticeable shaking, releasing stress over hours or days through slow fault movements that remain largely hidden from conventional monitoring systems.

phys-org.title: Water worries: The dangers of dehydration in pets
phys-org.description: The summer heat can be unrelenting, sending pets who usually run straight to their owners after being outside in search of their water bowls instead. Rehydrating after playtime is important, so if a pet does not have proper access—or a desire to seek out—water, the owner must step in before the companion's health is at risk.

phys-org.title: Carbon–bismuth bonds reveal that relativity blurs the textbook line between sigma and pi bonds
phys-org.description: Brown University chemists have provided direct evidence that upends the textbook explanation of how triple chemical bonds work in heavy elements. In a study published in Science, the researchers show evidence that when atomic nuclei are sufficiently heavy, the principles described in Einstein's theory of relativity change the structure of triple bonds—blurring the lines between the two separate types of bonds involved in textbook triple bonding.

phys-org.title: Why employee AI adoption isn't one-size-fits-all
phys-org.description: As artificial intelligence becomes more deeply embedded in everyday life and work, organizations are investing heavily in tools and employee training. But new research from Texas A&M University suggests a one-size-fits-all approach may miss a fundamental truth: People don't all respond to AI the same way.

phys-org.title: New catalyst could make mixed plastic waste recyclable in one chemical step
phys-org.description: Ever wondered where your plastics end up? A PET bottle can be washed, shredded, melted and given a second life. But most everyday items—toys, mattresses, car seats—are made from different plastics that refuse to mix when melted, producing unusable, contaminated material. Sorting is difficult and expensive, so most mixed plastic waste ends up burned or buried, and the materials are lost for good.

phys-org.title: Krill buildup could slow fin whale filter-feeding unless baleen stays 15% clear
phys-org.description: Usually there's safety in numbers, but it doesn't always work that way. Fin whales (Balaenoptera physalus) filter-feed on immense shoals of krill, engulfing colossal mouthfuls of water containing up to 144 kg of the crustaceans. But then the mighty creatures expel the water by squeezing it out through the racks of baleen lining their mouths.

phys-org.title: Programmable light simulates quantum matter across 300 processes without bigger circuits
phys-org.description: A team of researchers at the University of Ottawa and its Nexus for Quantum Technologies Institute, in collaboration with researchers from Federico II University in Italy, has developed a programmable quantum simulator that shapes a beam of light to replicate how particles move through complex materials, avoiding the need for ever-larger electronic hardware.

phys-org.title: Pre-cooked seafood-based meals can absorb chemical contaminants during packaging and processing
phys-org.description: Ready meals containing fish and seafood can expose consumers to chemical contaminants that are present in the environment or introduced during processing and packaging. A study by the Universitat Rovira i Virgili (URV) has, for the first time, analyzed the presence of a wide range of high-volume chemical substances in ready-made fish and seafood dishes sold in Tarragona, Spain.

phys-org.title: Quantum optics may turn this rare visual phenomenon into an eye test
phys-org.description: Modern life depends on quantum physics. It makes technologies such as GPS navigation, MRI scanners and computer chips possible. Now, the same science may also lead to a new way to test the health of our eyes. A University at Buffalo-led team has used a technique from quantum optics to make a little-known visual pattern produced inside the eye easier to see—potentially opening the door to a new way to test retinal health.

phys-org.title: From bursts to creep: Rewriting the story of mud volcano flows
phys-org.description: Mud volcanoes are often pictured as dramatic geological phenomena featuring the sudden eruption of large volumes of fiery mud in short, powerful bursts. By examining recent activity at the Lokbatan mud volcano in Azerbaijan, an international team of researchers led by the University of Oslo has found that many eruptions are relatively small and short-lived, producing only modest amounts of material near the crater.

phys-org.title: Neutron imaging reveals how water limits CO₂ storage in recycled concrete
phys-org.description: The construction sector faces two problems at once: it emits large amounts of CO₂ and produces vast quantities of concrete waste. But what if part of that waste could be used to trap carbon instead of ending up as rubble?

phys-org.title: Self-propelled microparticles scrub stubborn biofilms, improving wound care and instrument cleaning
phys-org.description: Newly developed microparticles can infiltrate stubborn bacterial matrices and release tiny oxygen bubbles to clean surfaces and wounds more efficiently than hydrogen peroxide or other cleaning agents alone, researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign report. In two papers, they have demonstrated the bubble-generating particles' ability to clean tenacious biofilms from surgical instruments, and—when embedded within bandages—to clean infected wounds and speed healing.

phys-org.title: Medieval Islamic societies considered lovesickness a distinct mental illness, research shows
phys-org.description: Lovesickness was taken seriously as a distinct mental illness by physicians in the medieval Islamic world, new research shows. Islamic scholars considered lovesickness, which they called ʿishq, to be different from melancholy—unlike Galen and other physicians from ancient Greece.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: An Athenian View of American Democracy
proj-syn.description: At 250, America is now producing a mindless, raw power and exponentially growing instability. The possibility of catharsis that characterized the United States at its bicentennial is hard to envisage a half-century later—to the detriment of us all.

proj-syn.title: Low-Cost Solutions to Maternal Mortality Already Exist
proj-syn.description: As foreign aid declines, policymakers in lower-income countries must increasingly focus on making better use of scarce resources. When it comes to maternal mortality, that means investing in simple, proven, and affordable interventions for postpartum hemorrhage, pre-eclampsia, and obstructed labor.

proj-syn.title: Postmodern Economics
proj-syn.description: Eschewing the idea of a single truth, the recently deceased English artist David Hockney showed that the world unfolds before us in ways we cannot fully understand. After long clinging to the pretense of certainty, economists would do well to embrace the same insight.

proj-syn.title: Digital Public Infrastructure Is Now a Strategic Battleground
proj-syn.description: Digital identity platforms, payment systems, and data exchanges promise more efficient, inclusive, and responsive public services. But in an era of geopolitical rivalry and concentrated digital power, those same systems create strategic dependencies that governments can no longer afford to ignore.

proj-syn.title: Should the Bank of Japan Raise Interest Rates?
proj-syn.description: At the beginning of 2013, when "Abenomics" was rolled out in Japan, the yen was significantly overvalued, and looser monetary policy was badly needed. Today, the opposite is true, indicating that interest-rate hikes may well be the right prescription for Japan.

proj-syn.title: How Argentina Can Protect Its Resource Wealth
proj-syn.description: Alaska, Norway, and Chile recognized the economic and political risks that accompany commodity booms and established sovereign wealth funds to preserve their resource revenues. Argentina’s hydrocarbon- and lithium-rich provinces should learn from their experience.

proj-syn.title: Reinventing Development Finance
proj-syn.description: Faced with shrinking concessional finance and rising borrowing costs, Rwanda has worked with the World Bank Group to leverage limited public funds and risk-sharing instruments to unlock private capital at scale and on affordable terms. It's an arrangement holding important lessons for low-income countries that must do more with less.

proj-syn.title: Mamdani’s American Dream
proj-syn.description: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s Independence Day address was a perfect example of ideology in the positive sense of the term. It overturned both the right-wing populist narrative of the United States and the left-wing "woke" critique with a vision that has the potential to mobilize a majority.

proj-syn.title: How Vulnerable Are US Financial Markets?
proj-syn.description: Fueled by more than $1 trillion in borrowed money and rising leverage across the financial system, US stock markets may have entered bubble territory. Two developments could trigger a sharp correction: higher interest rates and a loss of confidence in the handful of tech giants driving the AI boom.

proj-syn.title: Concessional Finance Is Needed More Than Ever
proj-syn.description: As debt burdens rise and climate shocks intensify, sustainable financing mechanisms are becoming indispensable. The Islamic Development Bank’s new concessional fund offers a promising model for mobilizing the resources needed to protect development gains and invest in resilience.

proj-syn.title: Ruling Class Clowns
proj-syn.description: By the end of the 19th-century in the US, it was clear to all interested observers that market power did not automatically or even easily translate into political capital and cultural authority. That is why, unlike the oligarchs of our time, certain Gilded Age capitalists learned how to become a ruling class.

proj-syn.title: The Missing Ingredient for European Tech Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: Europe’s dependence on US technology companies is both an economic challenge and a strategic vulnerability. The European Union’s new Tech Sovereignty Package is a step in the right direction, but without equally ambitious efforts to curb market concentration, it is bound to fall short.

proj-syn.title: In Praise of the World Cup’s Little Guys
proj-syn.description: In a world of great-power rivalry and hyper-scaling tech behemoths, you would be forgiven for thinking that the bulky bully always has the edge. But as this year's World Cup has shown repeatedly, you would be wrong.

proj-syn.title: Inside Ukraine’s Game-Changing Drone Industry
proj-syn.description: In recent months, Ukrainian drones have successfully struck dozens of sites deep inside Russia, targeting the oil industry, weapons plants, and logistics hubs. But while Ukraine has developed a world-leading military technology to defend itself from a much larger aggressor, drones will not be enough to end the war.

proj-syn.title: Just Say No to Remote Work
proj-syn.description: Even during the immediate post-pandemic period, when evidence on the labor-market effects of remote work was scant, there was a strong case to be made for going into the office, especially for younger workers. And now, multiple new studies have vindicated this intuition.

proj-syn.title: There Is Only One Acceptable Path for Designer Babies
proj-syn.description: Genetic-engineering tools with which to design one's progeny already exist, and they are being made even more potent with AI—at least for those who can afford such services. In the absence of policy interventions, we will be hurtling toward a tiered society in which economic privileges become biological advantages.

proj-syn.title: The Democratic Turkey NATO Needs
proj-syn.description: At NATO's upcoming summit in Ankara, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan will seek to portray his country as stable, confident, and essential to Western security. But only the last one is true, which is why the restoration of democracy in Turkey is more than a domestic concern.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup as It Should Be
proj-syn.description: While Donald Trump was widely expected to lord over this year’s World Cup, which the United States is co-hosting with Mexico and Canada, it has turned out not to be his scene. National teams populated with immigrants, and small-town America’s embrace of the event, go against everything Trump’s MAGA movement stands for.
